category_description: Buying, financing and selling a home in the United States.
subcategory_description: The size of mortgage that government-backed firms can buy.
label: Baseline conforming loan limit, one-unit property
context: In most of the United States. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are limited by law to buying mortgages at or below the conforming loan limit.

label: High-cost area ceiling, one-unit property
context: In areas where 115 percent of the local median home value exceeds the baseline, the limit is higher, up to a ceiling of 150 percent of the baseline.

label: Baseline limit in Alaska, Hawaii, Guam and the US Virgin Islands
context: Special statutory provisions set different limits for these four areas.

label: Ceiling in Alaska, Hawaii, Guam and the US Virgin Islands
context: The ceiling loan limit for one-unit properties in these four areas.

subject_intro: What the conforming loan limit is, how FHFA sets the baseline each year, and how higher limits apply in high-cost areas.
